solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Choosing to tour two states? American one presents deceptive appearance

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the word for choosing goes round the remaining pieces

parts.note: an option is a choice, the act of choosing
CAL is short for California, one US state
ILL is short for Illinois, a second US state
US is short for American, as in the United States
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A traveller weighing a two-state tour; then an American seemingly presents a false picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choosing' reads as a verb but gives a noun; 'to tour' has that noun wrap round the abbreviations for the two states, American and one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick of the eye that makes something look other than it is gives a deceptive appearance.

clue.text: Work free from undue ritual

indicators.note: set free, these three words are loosed from their order and recombined

explanation.surface: A plea to strip away excessive ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a literary work: Dickens's last completed novel. 'free' looks like part of the surface phrase 'free from'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a novel by Charles Dickens, so a creative work in the literary sense.

clue.text: Hardly flush though inebriated

definitions.meaning: short of money, as in money being ...

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash yet somehow drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means both stingy or short of cash and drunk.

clue.text: Recite lists going round circle; select one

indicators.note: the jumbled letters encircle the ring-shaped letter
to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does, so the letters of recite are knocked out of line

parts.note: O is the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: Instructions for choosing someone: read out lists while moving round a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a noun but is a verb: to lean over, signalling RECITE rearranged; 'going round' puts that around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a select group of people, and 'select one' reads as a select (exclusive) one.

clue.text: Byron learned perhaps to emulate him

definitions.text: Byron learned perhaps to emulate him

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the word learned could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Lord Byron studied someone so as to copy him.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero; Byron swam it in 1810 to show it could be done, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek lover famous for swimming the Hellespont is the figure Byron copied by swimming it himself.

clue.text: Angel's latest bad guy to be reformed. He's spotted with wings

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last one
reformed means re-formed, made into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angel's newest project is reforming a villain, who is then seen sprouting wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latest' takes the last letter of Angel's.
explanation.definitionFit: The red, black-spotted winged beetle (the American name for a ladybird) is spotted and has wings.

clue.text: They couldn't have helped Antony if you include name that's not deserved

indicators.note: the answer becomes the other word only once the extra letter is included, so it is that word minus the letter

parts.note: not earned, so undeserved

explanation.surface: Something about Mark Antony that seems to concern an undeserved name.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony asked 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'; people without ears could not lend them. Adding N gives UNEARNED, 'not deserved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no ears, such people could not answer Mark Antony's request to lend him their ears.

clue.text: I honour Charlie overlooking one line I see as fatuous

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece overlooking another sits above it, so first

parts.note: the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Roman numeral for one is I
I, and C for the letter that sounds like see

explanation.surface: Someone receiving an honour above Charlie lists what they find foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean silly or idiotic, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Breaking and entry was old crime first investigated here?

definitions.text: Breaking and entry was old crime first investigated here?

indicators.note: breaking the words apart lets their letters be reassembled
first takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A question about where a burglary from long ago was looked into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' signals the anagram of AND ENTRY WAS OLD plus C, crime's first letter. The Metropolitan Police headquarters is where a London crime would be investigated, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, where crimes such as a break-in would be investigated.

clue.text: Dexter could be chiefly relied upon

definitions.meaning: Latin and heraldic word for the right side
as in someone's most trusted assistant, their chief helper

explanation.surface: A man named Dexter may be the one most depended on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dexter' looks like a name but is the heraldic word for the right side; the second sense comes from the phrase 'right-hand man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter means on the right, and a right-hand man is the helper most depended upon.

clue.text: Joint one bends on bender

definitions.meaning: on a drinking spree, to bend this is to drink, as in the idiom bending it

explanation.surface: A joint, the part that keeps bending during a drinking binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' is a drinking spree, and 'bending the elbow' is an idiom for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the arm's middle joint, and the part that bends when a drinker lifts a glass.

clue.text: Still fighting fit and free to overcome resistance

indicators.note: overcome is read as come over, so the word for free covers the letter for resistance

parts.note: untied means loose or freed
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A fighter still in shape and at liberty to defeat opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not worn out remains fresh and ready, still in fighting form.

clue.text: Penniless tobacco picker could sew up pocket with this

indicators.note: to sew up is to rework, so the letters of the first words are remade into the answer together with the pocket

explanation.surface: A broke tobacco picker might mend his pocket with this.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus POCKET is an anagram of TOBACCO PICKER, with 'could sew up' as the signal. 'Boracic lint' is Cockney rhyming slang for skint, meaning broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Through rhyming slang (boracic lint for skint) the word means having no money.

clue.text: Fowler might be interested in this review of Modern English Usage headings

definitions.text: Fowler might be interested in this

indicators.note: a re-view is a new look, so the letters are viewed again in a fresh order
the headings of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: H. W. Fowler, author of Modern English Usage, might care about a review of its headings.
explanation.walkthrough: Fowler wrote Modern English Usage, but here a fowler is a bird hunter. 'review of' rearranges MEU, the headings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fowler is someone who hunts birds, so a large Australian bird might interest one.

clue.text: Dubious lender advanced roubles

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
R is the abbreviation for the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A shady moneylender has handed over some Russian cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doubtful or uncertain is not plain, so both words describe questionable matters.

clue.text: Aware of coins circulating in Colorado and all over United States

indicators.note: the shuffled coins sit inside the two state abbreviations

parts.note: CO is the postal abbreviation for Colorado

indicators.note: coins circulating move about, so their letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Knowing that money is passing round Colorado and the whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: To be awake to something is to be aware of it, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Atmosphere around Italy is essentially upmarket

indicators.note: the middle letters are placed around the letter for Italy
the essence of the word is its centre, so the middle letters

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: The mood in Italy is basically upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atmosphere around Italy' looks like one phrase; the parse splits it as 'Atmosphere' then 'around Italy is', with 'is' meaning 'is placed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere is the gas surrounding the earth, and the word can also mean a mood or feel.

clue.text: Choral Evensong maybe heals schism among the clergy — and creates new one

definitions.meaning: a broadcast service is the kind of programme in the religious slot on TV or radio
closing the gap between the words (healing the schism) makes one word, a new kind of lot

explanation.surface: A sung service mends a split among churchmen and starts a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heals schism' closes the gap in GOD'S LOT, the clergy; 'creates new one' adds that the joined word means a different lot, a broadcasting slot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the slang term for the time set aside for religious programmes on TV or radio, where Choral Evensong is broadcast.

clue.text: Feel under obligation to say nothing to caller

indicators.note: to someone who is calling, what is spoken is heard, not seen written

parts.note: O is the round symbol for zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Feeling bound not to say a word to a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say nothing' is to say the letter O, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in debt to someone is to be under an obligation to them.

clue.text: Light case for the Spanish Queen in northern Tunisia

parts.note: la is Spanish for the (feminine)

indicators.note: the royal letters go inside the northern and Tunisian letters

parts.note: TN is the international vehicle code for Tunisia
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A lamp casing for Spain's queen in the north of Tunisia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light case' is the definition; 'for' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp housing a flame inside a protective casing is literally a case for a light.

clue.text: Rabble-rousing leader leaves impression

indicators.note: the word's leading letter departs, so the first letter goes

parts.note: sedition is speech stirring up rebellion

explanation.surface: A demagogue walks out, leaving a strong impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader leaves' removes the S from SEDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, an impression is one print run of a book, much the same as an issue of it.

clue.text: International breaks jaw with greater style

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the word, splitting it

parts.note: to jaw is to chatter, to talk idly

explanation.surface: An international player fractures a jaw, but with more flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jaw' looks like a body part but is a verb, to chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart or dapper, so the comparative means dressed with more style.

clue.text: Wasn't she well matched and extremely energetic in caber tossing?

indicators.note: the outer letters go inside the scrambled word
a tossed caber spins over, so the letters are mixed up
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Highland Games question about a woman fit and energetic at the caber toss.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Rebecca was met at a well and chosen as Isaac's wife, so 'well matched' is a pun. 'in' sets the extremes of 'energetic' within the tossed caber.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical woman found at a well by Abraham's servant became Isaac's wife, so she was matched at a well.

clue.text: Point of no return: 1BC? No, possibly earlier — are you tuned in?

indicators.note: the spoken piece comes earlier, before the rearranged letters
listening to a radio tuned in, one hears the words spoken rather than written

parts.note: spoken, the two words sound like the letters R and U

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be ordered another way

parts.note: the digit 1 is read as the letter I, then B and C

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about a date: maybe 1 BC, or earlier?
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC, earlier than 1 BC. 'possibly' rearranges IBC and NO into BICON.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing this river committed Caesar to civil war, so its name means a step that cannot be undone.

clue.text: At the foot of mountain heat hazes

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: heat haze makes things shimmer and blur, so the letters are distorted

explanation.surface: Heat shimmering at the base of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean under or below, so something at the foot of a thing lies under it.

clue.text: Little fish even in 5

indicators.note: even letters are those in the second, fourth and sixth places

explanation.surface: A small fish, even inside 5.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' stands for the answer to 5 Down; its even letters give the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweetfish is a small edible fish of Japan and East Asia.

clue.text: Recipe that's cooked perfectly

indicators.note: cooked means doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to a T means perfectly, giving T

explanation.surface: A recipe whose dish turns out just right.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is an old term for a recipe, so the clue as a whole also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English the word meant a set of instructions for making a dish or medicine.

clue.text: Unwed, left in bed and, we forgot, wrapped up like babies

indicators.note: both pieces go into the word for bed
forgetting the two-letter pronoun drops it from the first word

explanation.surface: An unmarried couple in bed together, trussed up like infants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgot' drops the pronoun from 'Unwed'; 'in' tucks what remains, plus the letter for left, into the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies are bundled up, wrapped snugly in layers, in the familiar idiom.

clue.text: Fertilises boundary trees

definitions.meaning: treats soil with lime, as farmers do
a Roman frontier or border line, from Latin

explanation.surface: Something feeds the hedge trees along a field's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means spreads quicklime on land, a Roman frontier (limes), and lindens or citrus trees.

clue.text: Fungus from east on religious painting from east

indicators.note: read from the east means right to left in an across answer, so backwards

parts.note: an ikon is a religious image of the Orthodox Church

explanation.surface: A mushroom from the Orient growing on an Eastern icon.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-stemmed white Japanese mushroom is an edible fungus.

clue.text: After ache is treated intention is to reverse deficiency in blood supply

indicators.note: treated means processed or altered, so the letters are rearranged
the synonym is turned back to front

parts.note: an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: Once a pain has been seen to, the doctor plans to undo a circulation problem.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term names a restricted flow of blood to a part of the body.

clue.text: Liberal friends had since realigned with no vote

indicators.note: a liberal rendering is a free one, so the letters are freely rearranged
realigned means put in a new order, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Liberal supporters who have since changed allegiance lose their vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a party label but signals the anagram, with 'realigned' backing it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stripped of the right to vote is to lose the franchise, being without a ballot.
